title: North Point Wet Weather Facility
description: This water treatment facility was built in 1951 and today functions as a backup when rainy weather overwhelms the capacity of the other facilities in San Francisco.

title: Embarcadero SAFE Navigation Center
description: This homeless shelter can be used by up to 200 unhoused people, and offers intensive on-site services to help guide people into stable housing.

title: I-80 On-Ramp and Interchange
description: Nicknamed “The MacArthur Maze,” this section of the highway connects the Bay Bridge to I-80, I-580, and I-880, and local roads, serving over 100,000 drivers every day.

title: OAK Airport
description: In 2022 the Port of Oakland completed a 30 million dollar project to improve the perimeter dike of this airport, providing protection against sea level rise until the year 2060.

title: Palo Alto Horizontal Levee
description: As of 2026, construction on this nature-based levee has begun. It is designed to protect the marsh from sea level rise, act as a wildlife habitat, and filter wastewater.

title: Suisun Marsh
description: This recreational site and wildlife habitat is just downstream of one of California’s largest clean water supplies, making its health important to farmers and residents all over the state.
